# Grading rubric

This packaged reference is the runtime copy of the repository README's grading specification. Read it before assigning any grade.

## Claim-chain completeness ratings

Rate an atomic metric claim—a table cell—not a paper as a whole. For example:

| Model | Dataset 1 | Dataset 2 |
|---|---:|---:|
| SOTA1 | a1 | a2 |
| Ours | b1 | b2 |

This table contains four claims. `b1` and `b2` are <strong>self-model claims</strong> made for the paper's model; `a1` and `a2` are <strong>other-model claims</strong> cited or remeasured by the paper.

A paper may contain many experimental tables. Start with the most important few—typically the main results, decisive ablations, and central generalization tests—and register each important cell independently. Do not assign one global rating to the paper.

<sub>Prioritize ablations by reproduction cost. Ablations that add or remove model modules and therefore require retraining or new weights are usually lower priority than the main result. Ablations produced by changing only test-time settings, inference parameters, input conditions, or evaluator switches while reusing the same released checkpoint are low-cost and controllable, so they may be tested earlier. Each test-time variation still needs its own frozen protocol and must not be merged into the main-result metric chain.</sub>

### Two categories, four independent ratings

1. <strong>Delivery completeness:</strong> what the authors made available.
   - <strong>TD (Test Delivery Completeness):</strong> whether the authors delivered the weights, evaluation code, test data/split, and protocol needed to verify the value.
   - <strong>RD (Training Delivery Completeness):</strong> whether the authors delivered the training code, training data/split, settings, and dependent weights needed to produce the evaluated checkpoint.
2. <strong>Reproduction completeness:</strong> what an independent reproducer actually verified.
   - <strong>TR (Test Reproduction Completeness):</strong> how far the reproducer executed and audited the checkpoint-to-metric path.
   - <strong>RR (Training Reproduction Completeness):</strong> how far the reproducer executed and audited the raw-data-to-trained-checkpoint-to-metric path.

Delivery describes what the authors made available; reproduction describes what an independent reproducer actually verified. The ratings do not substitute for one another.

<strong>Delivery constrains reproduction:</strong> Reproduction completeness is bounded by delivery completeness: when critical materials required by the target chain are not fully delivered, reproduction normally cannot be complete. When grading reproduction, the reproducer may proactively locate the exact training dataset and split explicitly used by the paper when they are publicly available online, and may run training-data preprocessing according to rules already specified by the paper or official repository. These actions merely obtain or deterministically reconstruct materials whose identities are already defined, so they do not lower the reproduction grade. However, the reproducer need not complete training code that the authors did not deliver and should not guess training parameters, stopping conditions, or checkpoint-selection rules omitted by the paper or official repository. Instead, record each such condition as missing and grade reproduction accordingly. Results produced from a reproducer-written training implementation or guessed configuration may be reported as an independent implementation or independent-protocol result, but not as a strict reproduction of the target claim.

### Grade definitions

Grade each of the four dimensions independently; one generic table cannot be used to infer the others. The base grades, in ascending order, are `F`, `I`, `M`, `E`, and `O`. Use `M+` or `E+` when the evidence clearly exceeds the base requirements for `M` or `E` but does not reach the next base grade. The labels follow the “Failed / Improving / Medium / Excellent / Outstanding” naming scheme[[1](https://www.zhihu.com/question/495085246), [2](https://www.dingteam.com/article/285)], but here they separately measure <strong>the auditable basis provided by the release</strong> and <strong>the auditable evidence produced by actual reproduction</strong>. Delivery completeness depends only on what the authors released, regardless of whether a reproducer ran it, whether execution succeeded, or whether the resulting value matched. Reproduction completeness depends on what was actually executed and audited. Neither judges whether the value itself is high or low, nor extends to an overall credibility rating for the entire paper. `NR` means Not Rated / Not Applicable and is not a grade on this scale.

Every definition applies to one frozen claim. For example, “the model scores `b1=82.7` on `Dataset 1` in Table 1 of `Paper X`” is one claim; other cells in the same paper are graded separately.

#### TD: Test Delivery Completeness

Grade only the scope, specificity, and claim linkage of the authors' released materials; do not consider whether a reproducer ran them, whether execution succeeded, or whether a resulting value matched. Assign the <strong>highest grade supported by the materials</strong>, using a weakest-critical-link rule: completeness elsewhere cannot compensate for a critical gap in checkpoint identity, test split, or evaluation rules.

| Grade | Definition | Example (`Paper X / b1=82.7`) |
|---|---|---|
| <strong>O</strong> | 1. The test runtime environment and version numbers;<br>2. model weights that exactly match the target claim;<br>3. the paper's test set and exact split;<br>4. all test-time parameters;<br>5. clear and complete test rules (including data preprocessing, inference, evaluation, aggregation, and randomness handling), with no result-affecting setting left to guess or substitute. | The authors provide `environment.yml` specifying Python 3.10.13, PyTorch 2.1.2, and CUDA 12.1. Table 1 is explicitly tied to `paper-x-step-50000.ckpt`, whose SHA-256 is supplied, and `test_ids.txt` lists all 10,000 evaluated sample IDs. The test command sets `seed=42` and `batch_size=64`; images are resized to 256 pixels and center-cropped to 224×224; the released `accuracy.py` explicitly defines top-1 accuracy over all samples and ties that computation to the reported `82.7`. |
| <strong>E</strong> | 1. The checkpoint, test set and split, test parameters, and test rules tied to the claim are delivered;<br>2. every setting that affects result interpretation is explicit;<br>3. only limited operational information that does not change the test protocol is absent, such as an example launch command or the exact version of a noncritical dependency.<br><strong>Award E+ when:</strong><br>1. These materials are directly locatable, versioned, and explicitly tied to the claim;<br>2. only one noncritical operational detail is absent;<br>3. no result-affecting setting is left for the reproducer to supply. | <strong>E:</strong> The authors provide `paper-x-step-50000.ckpt`, all 10,000 sample IDs, `seed=42`, the 224×224 center-crop rule, and `accuracy.py`, but omit a complete launch command and do not pin versions for noncritical logging tools.<br><strong>E+:</strong> All those materials are versioned and explicitly tied to Table 1; only the exact GPU model is omitted, which does not change the disclosed test protocol. |
| <strong>M</strong> | 1. Major parts of the checkpoint, test data, inference code, or evaluator are delivered, but at least one critical delivery is incomplete;<br>2. the checkpoint version, exact test split, key inference parameter, evaluator, or aggregation rule is missing or ambiguous;<br>3. the materials define only part of the test chain, or define a complete chain that cannot be strictly tied to the paper's original protocol.<br><strong>Award M+ when:</strong><br>1. Every checkpoint-to-metric stage has corresponding materials;<br>2. the weights, test set, and evaluation method broadly match the claim;<br>3. only one limited item—such as the original seed, exact dependency version, secondary test parameter, or statistical detail—is missing. | <strong>M:</strong> The authors release only `table1_predictions.json` and `accuracy.py`, but not the checkpoint that generated the predictions; alternatively, the repository contains both `test-v1.txt` and `test-v2.txt` without identifying which one belongs to Table 1.<br><strong>M+:</strong> The authors release `paper-x-step-50000.ckpt`, `test_ids.txt`, and `accuracy.py`, and specify a 224×224 center crop and `batch_size=64`, but omit the seed used for Table 1. |
| <strong>I</strong> | 1. Only the paper value, repository, weight URL, data entry point, or scattered code can be found;<br>2. critical artifacts are severely incomplete or the available artifacts cannot be tied together;<br>3. no executable claim-level test chain can yet be formed. | The repository links only a weight named `model_final.ckpt`, with no configuration or table mapping that ties it to Table 1. The `Dataset 1` website offers multiple test splits, but the repository selects none of them and provides no evaluation command. |
| <strong>F</strong> | 1. Released artifacts are confirmed to conflict with the target claim—for example, the weight belongs to another model variant, a different test split is used, or the evaluation protocol was substituted;<br>2. even if these materials run, their result cannot be attributed to the target claim. | The download page labels `paper-x-large.ckpt` as the Table 1 weight, but its configuration has `hidden_size=768`, whereas the Table 1 Large model requires `hidden_size=1024`; its test result therefore cannot be attributed to `b1=82.7`. |

#### RD: Training Delivery Completeness

Grade only the scope, specificity, and claim linkage of the authors' released materials; do not consider whether a reproducer trained the model, produced a checkpoint, or matched the paper's test result. Assign the <strong>highest grade supported by the materials</strong>, using a weakest-critical-link rule: complete code or environment configuration cannot compensate for a core gap in training data, dependent weights, or key training parameters.

| Grade | Definition | Example (`Paper X / b1=82.7`) |
|---|---|---|
| <strong>O</strong> | 1. The training runtime environment and version numbers;<br>2. the training data and exact split;<br>3. dependent weights and initialization materials;<br>4. all training parameters, stopping conditions, and checkpoint-selection rules;<br>5. clear and complete training rules (including data preprocessing, sampling, optimization, distributed training, and randomness handling), with no result-affecting setting left to guess or substitute. | The authors provide `environment.yml` specifying Python 3.10.13, PyTorch 2.1.2, and CUDA 12.1. `train_ids.txt` and `val_ids.txt` list 1,200,000 training and 50,000 validation samples, and training starts from `base-vit-b16.ckpt` with a supplied SHA-256. `train.yaml` specifies `batch_size=4096`, `lr=1e-3`, AdamW, cosine scheduling, `seed=42`, and 300 epochs, and selects the best checkpoint by validation top-1 accuracy. `train.py` and the documentation define image augmentation, sampling, and eight-GPU distributed training. |
| <strong>E</strong> | 1. The training data and split, model configuration, dependent weights, training parameters, and training rules are delivered and tied to the target claim;<br>2. every setting that affects training meaning or checkpoint selection is explicit;<br>3. only limited operational information that does not change the training protocol is absent, such as an example launch command or the exact version of a noncritical dependency.<br><strong>Award E+ when:</strong><br>1. These materials are directly locatable, versioned, and explicitly tied to the claim;<br>2. only one noncritical operational detail is absent;<br>3. no setting affecting training-result interpretation is left for the reproducer to supply. | <strong>E:</strong> The authors provide `train.py`, `train.yaml`, `base-vit-b16.ckpt`, and all sample IDs, but `train_ids.txt` must be deterministically generated with the released `make_split.py --version 2.1`.<br><strong>E+:</strong> The data split, base-model hash, all hyperparameters, stopping condition, and checkpoint-selection rule are directly provided and explicitly tied to Table 1; only the exact models of the eight GPUs are omitted. |
| <strong>M</strong> | 1. Major parts of the training data, training code, model configuration, or dependent weights are delivered, but at least one critical delivery is incomplete;<br>2. the exact data split, initialization materials, key hyperparameters, stopping conditions, or checkpoint-selection rule is missing or ambiguous;<br>3. the materials define only part of the training chain, or define a complete chain that cannot be strictly tied to the paper's original training protocol.<br><strong>Award M+ when:</strong><br>1. Every data-to-checkpoint stage has corresponding materials;<br>2. the model, primary training data, and training method broadly match the claim;<br>3. only limited information such as the original seed, exact dependency version, secondary hyperparameter, or statistical detail is missing. | <strong>M:</strong> The authors release training code and the `Dataset 1` download location, but not the training-sample split, and do not state whether initialization uses `base-vit-b16.ckpt` or random weights.<br><strong>M+:</strong> The authors provide training IDs, the base model, `train.py`, and primary hyperparameters, covering every data-to-checkpoint stage, but omit the seed and number of warmup steps. |
| <strong>I</strong> | 1. Only a paper description, code repository, data entry point, or scattered training code can be found;<br>2. the training data, exact split, key dependent weights, model configuration, or training entry point is critically incomplete, or the available artifacts cannot be tied together;<br>3. no executable target-training chain can yet be formed. | The repository contains only the model architecture and data loader. The `Dataset 1` training split, training entry point, optimizer configuration, and base-model link are absent, so the target training chain cannot be formed from the release. |
| <strong>F</strong> | 1. Training artifacts are confirmed to conflict with the target claim—for example, the code or configuration belongs to another model, a different training-data version is used, or the training protocol was substituted;<br>2. even if these materials run, the resulting checkpoint cannot be attributed to the target claim. | The repository labels `train_large.yaml` as the Table 1 Large configuration, but it specifies `hidden_size=768` while the paper defines `1024`. The configuration belongs to another model and cannot deliver the training chain for the target Table 1 checkpoint. |

#### TR: Test Reproduction Completeness

Grade the testing actually completed and the evidence retained. `TR` jointly considers protocol alignment, execution coverage, and agreement between the reproduced value and the paper's claim; a nearby value cannot compensate for misaligned weights, data, or protocol. Using a different but compatible CUDA, driver, or hardware version because of local constraints is not a deduction when the change is documented and does not alter computation semantics, precision mode, or metric results.

| Grade | Definition | Example (`Paper X / b1=82.7`) |
|---|---|---|
| <strong>O</strong> | 1. Use the test environment and version configuration specified by the paper or official repository, or a compatible environment verified not to change computation semantics, precision mode, or metric results;<br>2. use model weights that exactly match the target claim;<br>3. run on the paper's specified test set and exact split;<br>4. strictly follow the execution method, parameter configuration, and metric computation specified by the paper or official repository;<br>5. after the complete end-to-end test, obtain a metric consistent with the paper's claimed value, with error no greater than a preregistered, very small tolerance;<br>6. retain the actual commands, run logs, per-item results, and final metric so both the execution and numeric conclusion are auditable. | In the authors' Python 3.10.13, PyTorch 2.1.2, and CUDA 12.1 environment, the SHA-256-verified `paper-x-step-50000.ckpt` is evaluated on all 10,000 IDs in `test_ids.txt` using `seed=42`, `batch_size=64`, a 224×224 center crop, and `accuracy.py`. The resulting top-1 accuracy is `82.69`; under the paper's one-decimal reporting rule, it matches the claimed `82.7`. Commands, logs, and per-item predictions are retained. |
| <strong>E</strong> | 1. Use model weights tied to the target claim and the paper's complete test set;<br>2. complete the full end-to-end test and obtain a valid result using the paper's metric computation;<br>3. retain and document only limited incompleteness or differences in parameters, repetition count, or test rules that do not change the task or metric meaning;<br>4. obtain a value close to the paper's claim, or a difference reasonably explained by the documented protocol differences;<br>5. retain commands, logs, per-item results, and protocol-deviation records.<br><strong>Award E+ when:</strong><br>1. The weights, test set, execution method, parameters, and metric computation are strictly aligned with the paper, and the runtime is either the specified environment or a verified-equivalent compatible environment;<br>2. the complete end-to-end test and evidence retention are complete;<br>3. the reproduced value differs by more than O's very small tolerance, preventing an O grade, or only one operational evidence item that does not affect interpretation is absent. | <strong>E:</strong> The Table 1 checkpoint is evaluated on all 10,000 test samples using the authors’ preprocessing and `accuracy.py`. The paper reports the mean of five runs with `seed=40–44`, but compute constraints permit only `seed=42`; it gives `82.6`, close to the claimed `82.7`.<br><strong>E+:</strong> The environment, checkpoint, sample list, `seed=42`, preprocessing, and `accuracy.py` strictly match the authors’ setup, but the complete run gives `82.4`, outside the preregistered `±0.1` tolerance. It therefore cannot earn O, although commands, logs, and per-item results are fully retained. |
| <strong>M</strong> | 1. Complete a valid partial test chain, such as one-sample or fixed-subset inference, [evaluator replay](#evaluator-replay), or a full test under a substitute protocol;<br>2. at least one of the model weights, test split, key parameters, or metric computation cannot be strictly tied to the paper;<br>3. obtain an auditable partial or independent-protocol result that cannot be treated as a reproduction of the paper's claimed value;<br>4. record the actual materials, commands, and major protocol differences.<br><strong>Award M+ when:</strong><br>1. Use weights tied to the claim and complete a full run on the complete test set;<br>2. broadly align the primary execution method and metric computation with the paper;<br>3. use preregistered independent settings only because limited information—such as the author's seed, exact dependency version, secondary parameter, or statistical detail—is unavailable;<br>4. retain complete results and deviation records, while strict numeric alignment remains impossible. | <strong>M:</strong> No usable checkpoint exists, so the released `table1_predictions.json` is passed to `accuracy.py`, recovering `82.7`; only the scoring stage is reproduced.<br><strong>M+:</strong> The Table 1 checkpoint is evaluated on all 10,000 samples, but the authors did not release the seed. The reproducer preregisters `seed=42`, obtains `82.5`, and fully records this protocol difference. |
| <strong>I</strong> | 1. Begin actual testing and complete at least one of environment startup, code import, model loading, data loading, or evaluator-interface checking;<br>2. encounter a blocker in missing artifacts, configuration, dependencies, or resources;<br>3. obtain no valid metric result capable of judging the target claim;<br>4. record the failure point, error logs, and current blockers. | The conda environment is created and `paper-x-step-50000.ckpt` loads successfully, but data loading reveals that `test_ids.txt` is missing. The 10,000 samples used by the paper cannot be identified, so no metric is computed; the error log and missing item are recorded. |
| <strong>F</strong> | 1. Confirm that a completed run used the wrong model weights, test split, key parameters, or metric computation, or that its outputs have an irreparable integrity failure;<br>2. invalidate the run so its value cannot be attributed to the target claim;<br>3. explicitly record the invalidation reason and supporting evidence. | After evaluation, configuration inspection shows that the loaded `paper-x-base.ckpt` has `hidden_size=768`, while the Table 1 Large model requires `hidden_size=1024`. The resulting `79.3` is invalidated, with the weight path, configuration, and invalidation reason recorded. |

<strong>TR numeric agreement and O-grade rule:</strong> Before execution, declare an absolute or relative tolerance based on the paper's reporting precision, metric variability, and domain convention. Treat the reproduced and reported values as consistent when their difference does not exceed that tolerance; if the paper reports only a limited number of decimal places, values that become equal when rounded to the same precision may also be treated as consistent. For example, if the paper reports `82.7` and the preregistered absolute tolerance is `±0.1`, then `82.69` is consistent with `82.7`, whereas `82.4` has an absolute error of `0.3`, exceeds the tolerance, and is inconsistent. The tolerance must not be relaxed after seeing the result merely to obtain a match. `TR-O` requires both a strictly aligned test protocol and numeric agreement. If a complete, strict test differs by more than the preregistered tolerance, it cannot earn `TR-O`; grade it at another level according to execution and evidence completeness, and separately record the numeric outcome as `not_matched` or `contradicted_under_pinned_protocol`. Conversely, falling within tolerance cannot compensate for misaligned weights, data, or protocol.

#### RR: Training Reproduction Completeness

<strong>Compute eligibility:</strong> Before assigning an `RR` grade, compare the locally available compute resources with the training resources stated by the paper or official repository. If local compute is below the stated training requirement, skip training reproduction, do not assign an `RR` grade, and record `NR`. Do not reduce the model, training data, training duration, or precision requirements merely to fit local compute and then retain an `RR` grade for the original claim. If such an experiment is useful, register it as a separate independent-protocol result rather than a training reproduction of the target claim.

| Grade | Definition | Example (`Paper X / b1=82.7`) |
|---|---|---|
| <strong>O</strong> | 1. Use the training environment and version configuration specified by the paper or official repository, or a compatible environment verified not to change training semantics, precision mode, or result interpretation;<br>2. use the same model initialization as the paper, whether training from scratch or starting from the specified base model, pretrained weights, and initialization configuration;<br>3. use the paper's specified training set and exact split;<br>4. strictly follow the training algorithm, training method, and full configuration claimed by the paper or official repository, including data processing, sampling, optimization, learning-rate scheduling, distributed training, randomness handling, stopping conditions, and checkpoint-selection rules;<br>5. complete end-to-end training and produce new model weights;<br>6. evaluate the newly trained model under the paper's specified test protocol and obtain a metric consistent with the paper's claimed value, with error no greater than a preregistered, very small tolerance;<br>7. retain training and test commands, logs, data and dependent-weight identities, key checkpoints, per-item test results, and the final metric so the complete model-initialization-to-paper-metric chain is auditable. | In the authors’ Python 3.10.13 and PyTorch 2.1.2 environment, training starts from the SHA-256-verified `base-vit-b16.ckpt`, uses all 1,200,000 samples in `train_ids.txt`, follows `train.yaml` for 300 epochs on eight GPUs, and selects the newly produced `epoch-287.ckpt` by validation top-1 accuracy. Evaluation under the Table 1 protocol gives `82.68`; under the paper’s one-decimal reporting rule, it matches the claimed `82.7`. Training and test commands, logs, checkpoints, and per-item results are retained. |
| <strong>E</strong> | Training data and split, model configuration, training parameters, dependent weights, stopping conditions, and checkpoint-selection rules are frozen; end-to-end training, full testing, and training-trajectory audit are complete, with at most minor traceable compatibility handling that does not change training meaning.<br><strong>Award E+ when:</strong> preregistered independent training repetitions or uncertainty analysis are also complete and data, checkpoint, and aggregation identities are checked; only clean-environment reconstruction or the evidence needed for direct third-party audit remains absent. | <strong>E:</strong> Training and full evaluation use the same base model, complete training set, algorithm, and primary hyperparameters. The paper reports the mean of five trainings with `seed=40–44`, but compute permits only `seed=42`; the new model gives `82.6`.<br><strong>E+:</strong> Initialization, data, training configuration, checkpoint selection, and test protocol are strictly aligned, but the complete training gives `82.3`, outside the preregistered `±0.1` tolerance. The chain and evidence are complete, but the value does not qualify for O. |
| <strong>M</strong> | Part of a valid training chain was executed, or one training run and evaluation were completed while key conditions could not be strictly aligned with the paper—for example, only short-step or subset smoke training was completed, or data, seeds, scale, hyperparameters, or stopping rules differed materially.<br><strong>Award M+ when:</strong> one end-to-end training and full test were completed under a substantially aligned protocol, with only limited information affecting strict alignment missing or repeated training/uncertainty analysis still incomplete. | <strong>M:</strong> Only the first 10,000 training samples are used for five epochs, showing decreasing loss and producing a loadable checkpoint; this cannot represent the paper’s full training.<br><strong>M+:</strong> Full 300-epoch training and complete testing use the full dataset and same base model, but the authors omit the number of learning-rate warmup steps. The reproducer preregisters 10 epochs, obtains `81.9`, and records the deviation. |
| <strong>I</strong> | Materials were audited or training attempted, but critical data, configuration, dependency, or resource problems still block progress, and no valid checkpoint suitable for full evaluation exists. | The environment and data loader work, but checksum verification fails for the downloaded `base-vit-b16.ckpt`. Training stops during initialization and no evaluable new checkpoint is produced; the error log and blocker are retained. |
| <strong>F</strong> | The executed training is confirmed to have used the wrong data, model configuration, or training protocol. The resulting checkpoint and result are invalidated and cannot be attributed to the target claim. | After training and evaluation, the run is found to have used `train-v1.txt` while the target claim explicitly uses `train-v2.txt`. The new model’s `80.1` cannot be attributed to Table 1 `b1`; the run is invalidated and the reason recorded. |


### Rating example

| Claim | Type | TD | RD | TR | RR | Outcome |
|---|---|:---:|:---:|:---:|:---:|---|
| `b1` | self-model | E | M+ | E+ | M | matched |
| `b2` | self-model | M | I | M | NR | not_strictly_comparable |
| `a1` | other-model | M | NR | M | NR | author_table_only |
| `a2` | other-model | F | NR | F | NR | invalidated |

- <strong>`b1`:</strong> Exact weights, test set and evaluator were released and replayed; training data requires a public reconstruction script, and only a training subset has run.
- <strong>`b2`:</strong> Weights are public, but seeds and the full test split are missing; training data is unavailable. Only an independent fixed-protocol result is defensible.
- <strong>`a1`:</strong> The current paper did not rerun SOTA1; it copied the original paper's number. Audit the SOTA1 paper separately.
- <strong>`a2`:</strong> SOTA1 used a different dataset split from Ours although both appear in the same comparison column.

For other-model claims, also record whether the value was `cited_from_original_paper`, `rerun_by_current_authors`, or `unclear`. Only an actual rerun under the same protocol belongs directly to the current table's test chain; copying a cited number is not a reproduction by the current authors.

## Glossary

<a id="evaluator-replay"></a>
<strong>Evaluator replay</strong> means recalculating a paper's score from the authors' released outputs and evaluation code. For example, the authors release 1,000 generated videos and the VBench code; rerunning it gives `81.0`, matching the paper's `81.0`. This shows only that the scoring process is reproducible—not that the model generation or training process is reproducible.

<a id="api-call"></a>
<strong>Changing an API call</strong> means adapting obsolete function names, argument names, or call syntax to a newer dependency without changing the supplied values or computation. For example, replace the old `torch_device="cuda"` argument with the new `device="cuda"` argument.

<a id="independent-seed"></a>
<strong>Reproducer-chosen seeds</strong> are seeds selected by the reproducer when the authors do not release the original ones—for example, `42, 43, 44, 45, 46`. They should be fixed and recorded before running to prevent selecting only favorable results afterward. Because they are not the authors' original seeds, the run is not an exact recovery of the original experiment.

<a id="protocol"></a>
A <strong>protocol</strong> is the fixed set of choices used to produce and score a metric, such as the test split, input preprocessing, inference steps, seeds, sample count, and scoring method. Renaming a legacy API argument does not change the protocol; using a different test set or number of inference steps does.
